newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Jan 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A spokesman for Federal Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp refused to comment on a Sun-Herald report that the Government was considering raising the minimum age superannuation can be accessed in the May Budget. The report says the minimum age of access to supernnuation may be raised from 55 to 60 to encourage private savings and the Government may also limit the amount of superannuation that could be taken as a lump sum. Page 2.

Democrat leader Cheryl Kernot called on all tax reform possibilities, including a GST, to be discussed. Speaking at the Democrats' national conference on the weekend, Kernot said tax subsidies should be cut to help revenue. Kernot joins Woolworths managig director Reg Clairs and Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett in calling for discussion on tax reform. Page 4.

The Federal Government's new human rights legislation may deter people from seeking damages for discrimination, say lawyers and human rights lobbyists. The new law bars "representative actions" by trade unions, allowing only "persons aggrieved" to take acion in the Federal Court. The Law Institute of Victoria wrote a letter to Federal Attorney General Daryl Williams criticising the legislation.

Australia is set to be a major beneficiary of global tourism and travel, with an estimated 274,000 new jobs by 2007. These predictions, from the World Travel and Tourism Council summit in Portugal, have prompted a A$400,000 pilot study by the Federal Government into satellite accounting for travel and tourism. Satellite accounting techniques have been used by the council to predict 100 million new jobs in travel and tourism over the next decade.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As alleged paedophile Phillip Bells' lawyer Jim Boyens said Bell was in good spirits and wished to return home to Australia to clear his name, Bell will return to court in South Africa tonight to face the beginning of extradition proceedings to bring him ack to Australia to face over 200 charges of child molestation involving 29 boys. Page 1.

In a plan that should substantially increase Federal and State compensation bills, the States and Territories will ask Prime Minister John Howard to pare back native title rights to traditional hunting and fishing rights. As Queensland Premier Rob Borbide was last night locked in talks with West Australian Premier Richard Court, it is believed he is the only mainland conservative leader with reservations about this proposal. Page 1.

Federal Employment, Education, Training and Youth Affairs Minister Amanda Vanstone yesterday admitted that the Federal Government's increased Higher Education Contribution Scheme fees have contributed to a drop in cut-off scores for undergraduate science-elated courses. However, Vanstone defended HECS and said the drop in cut off scores reflected a four-year trend.

The women's competition at the Australian Tennis Open in Melbourne recieved a gush of fresh air over the weekend, with South African Amanda Coetzer defeating No. 1 seed Steffi Graf 6-2, 7-5. Others seeds already out of the competition are No.2 seed Aranta Sanchez Vicario, No. 3 Conchita Martinez, No. 5 Anke Huber and No. 7 Lindsay Davenport. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A major report into the future of the ABC by former head of Optus and Fairfax Bob Mansfield will recommend that it contract out most of its television drama and documentary production to the private sector and cut the 50-year-old overseas short wave radio service Radio Australia. Both moves would lead to big job losses at the national broadcaster. Page 1.

Suspected pedophile Philip Bell said from his jail cell in Port Elizabeth, South Africa, that he was not afraid to stand trial in Australia. If Bell is successfully returned to New South Wales, he will face over 200 criminal charges arising from complains by 29 individuals. Page 1.

As world number one women's tennis player Steffi Graf felt the heat from the surface of the Melbourne Park tennis court where she was playing in the Australian Open, she also felt troubled within as her father's court verdict on tax evasion charges contined, and finally lost a match to South African Amanda Coetzer 6-2, 7-5. Page 1.

Dr John Walker, the head of the New South Wales Malaria Register and a senior lecturer in the Department of Medicine at the University of Sydney, says there was a record number of malaria cases reported in the State last year, with at least two people dyig out of the 260 infected while travelling overseas. Page 1.
THE AGE

A Cabinet submission by the Attorney-General's Department anticipating last month's High Court Wik decision, warned that any legislation to extinguish native title on pastoral leases would be open to legal challenges and could result in massive compensatin claims. Such changes to legislation would not align with the Racial Discrimination Act, and some legislative options would breach the implied constitutional guarantee of equality before the law. Page A1.

The Transport Accident Commission will run a series of radio advertisements next month in an effort to halt aggressive driving, also known as "road rage". TAC general manager of marketing, Ian Forsyth, said the Commission concluded that stress and a lackof time were the main causes of road rage. Page A1.

Key university administrators have called for an inquiry into tertiary entrance rank cut-off scores, saying they often have no meaning and can be manipulated to protect the reputations of some courses. Science courses, and, to a lesser extent, engineering courses have had their figures manipulated this year because of a fall in the quality and number of applicants. Page A1.

Number one women's tennis player Steffi Graf bowed out of the fourth round of the Ford Australian Tennis Open yesterday to South African Amanda Coetzer in a game that was so hot, Graf had her trainer apply ice to the back of her neck at every change of ends. Graf joined several other seeds out of the tournament at the end of a fiery weekend of tennis. Page A1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
